ogTitle: Ranong to Phang Nga — Driving Thailand's Andaman Coast
ogDesc: Drive Highway 4 from Ranong down to Phang Nga past waterfalls, old towns and Khao Lak, ending at Phang Nga Bay and James Bond Island — an unhurried 3-day, 2-night trip that actually works.
h1:
Ranong to Phang Nga
Down the Andaman Coast
intro: Ranong and Phang Nga sit on the same road — Phetkasem (Highway 4), which runs south along the Andaman coast. If you've made it to Ranong and aren't ready to head home yet, carrying on down to Phang Nga makes for a tidy trip, because the road in between has waterfalls, viewpoints and old towns, and it all ends at Khao Lak and Phang Nga Bay — the sea and limestone islands that people travel from all over the world to see. This plan is built as 3 days and 2 nights, easy to self-drive and unhurried. All distances and prices are rough estimates, so double-check them before you set off.

blocks.html: From Ranong town to Phang Nga town is around 230 kilometres — about 3.5 hours if you drive straight through. But the charm of this route is that there's something to stop for along the way, so it's better to break it into stages than to power through in one go. This plan splits it over three days: day one picks up Ranong's morning highlights then eases south, day two takes on Khao Lak and Thap Lamu, and day three closes out at Phang Nga Bay before everyone goes their separate ways. If you have less time, trim it to 2 days and 1 night — just pick the legs you most want to keep.

items: Self-drive travellers who want a one-way route they don't have to backtrack on — drive in one direction and you're done.
People already in Ranong who want to add Phang Nga's beaches onto the same trip.
Nature and beach lovers who enjoy waterfalls, forest and limestone islands out in the bay.
Anyone with 3 days or more who doesn't want to rush, and would rather stop to eat and take photos along the way.

blocks.title: Before you set off
blocks.html: This stretch of the Andaman coast gets a lot of rain. The clear-sky, calm-sea window is November to April. The Surin and Similan island groups only open from mid-November to mid-May — outside that the national parks are closed and you can't go out to the islands at all. If you're set on an island day, check the parks' latest opening and closing dates before you plan around them.

blocks.text: The route and distances at a glance

blocks.html: The whole trip runs mainly on Phetkasem (Highway 4). You head south from Ranong through Kapoe, cross into Phang Nga province at Khura Buri district, then work your way down through Takua Pa and Khao Lak to Phang Nga town. The main stops line up along the road like this:

items: Ranong → Khura Buri — about 120 km, roughly 1 hr 40 min driving. This is the first town across the Phang Nga line, and the pier for the Surin Islands is here.
Khura Buri → Khao Lak/Thap Lamu — about 85 km, roughly 1 hr 15 min, passing the old town of Takua Pa on the way.
Khao Lak → Phang Nga town — about 60 km, roughly 1 hr, turning onto the inland road toward Phang Nga Bay.
Total route — about 230 km; roughly 3 hr 30 min if you drive straight through, but this plan spreads it over 3 days.

blocks.text: Day 1 — A Ranong morning, then an easy drive to Khura Buri

blocks.html: No need to rush on day one. Grab breakfast and the Ranong highlights that sit right on the road south, then drive at an easy pace and overnight around Khura Buri, or carry on to Takua Pa. It depends on whether you plan to head out to the Surin Islands the next day.

items.activity: Dim sum breakfast in Ranong town — Ranong Ocha or Pi Ton
items.note: Fuel up before you hit the road. Ranong dim sum is known for its har gow and steamed buns, and it fills up fast.

items.activity: Stop at Ngao Waterfall, right off Phetkasem before you leave town
items.note: You can see the falls from the roadside. Park, take a few photos and have a short walk — there's plenty of water after the rainy season.

items.activity: Drive south through Kapoe district, stop at Baan Rai I Arun cafe if you fancy a break
items.note: A farm cafe set in a garden in the forest, with a stream and photo spots. It's just before the Phang Nga line.

items.activity: Cross into Phang Nga at Khura Buri, lunch at a made-to-order or seafood spot in town
items.note: Khura Buri is a small, quiet district, but it's the gateway out to the Surin Islands.

items.activity: Wander Khura Buri pier, take in the mangroves and the fishing-village feel
items.note: If you're heading out to the Surin Islands tomorrow, sort out the tour and check boat times today.

items.activity: Check in around Khura Buri, or drive on to Takua Pa
items.note: Choose based on tomorrow's plan. For an island day, stay near Khura Buri pier; if you're skipping the islands, you can drive on.

items.activity: A light dinner, then rest up and save your energy for tomorrow
items.note: Places around here close early, so it's easier to find food before nightfall.

blocks.title: About the Surin and Similan island trips
blocks.html: Boats to the Surin Islands leave from Khura Buri pier, around 50 minutes to an hour out. The Similans leave from Thap Lamu pier at Khao Lak. Both only open from mid-November to mid-May, and you can book day trips out and back. If you're set on an island day, set aside a full day for it and push the Khao Lak section to the following day.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Takua Pa old town, plus Khao Lak and Thap Lamu

blocks.html: This is the beach day of the trip. In the morning, stop by Takua Pa old town, which has Sino-Portuguese buildings a bit like Phuket's but with fewer people, then head into Khao Lak in the afternoon for the long beach and sunset. If you want to go out to the Similans, swap this in as a full day instead.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Old town → Khao Lak beach → Thap Lamu

items.activity: Walk Takua Pa old town (Si Takua Pa Road), the old buildings and local coffee shops
items.note: A Sino-Portuguese quarter that the crowds haven't fully found yet — pleasant for photos in the morning before the sun gets harsh.

items.activity: Drive into Khao Lak, check in at a beachfront stay
items.note: Khao Lak's beach runs for several kilometres, with both lively and quiet stretches — pick to suit your style.

items.activity: Seafood lunch — Sam Si Seafood in the Bang Sak area
items.note: A well-known spot on the main road, strong on fresh seafood — crab fried rice, seafood tom yum, fish fried with fish sauce.

items.activity: Sea-view cafe — Cotton Cafe at La Vela, or Valhalla
items.note: Get out of the afternoon sun with a coffee by the sea. Cotton is known for croissants, Valhalla for the view — seating is limited.

items.activity: Swim and walk the beach in the late afternoon, wait for sunset
items.note: This beach faces west, so you get a nice sea sunset when the sky's clear.

items.activity: Dinner at Krachang Khao Lak, a floating seafood spot at Thap Lamu pier
items.note: A floating restaurant with mangrove and mountain views, open 15:00–22:00, closed Tuesdays — check before you go.

blocks.title: Khao Lak and the tsunami memory
blocks.html: Khao Lak was hit hard by the 2004 tsunami. There's the memorial to Police Boat T.813, which the waves carried hundreds of metres inland from the sea, and a small museum to visit. Many people stop here to understand the area's story, not just for the beach.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Phang Nga Bay, Ko Tapu, Ko Panyi, then onward

blocks.html: On the last day you take the inland road into Phang Nga town and board a boat to see Phang Nga Bay — a sheltered sea ringed by oddly shaped limestone peaks. The highlights are Ko Tapu (James Bond Island) and Ko Panyi, a fishing village built out over the water. End the trip here and carry on to Phuket or Krabi if you like, since they're both close by now.

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Phang Nga Bay → Ko Tapu → Ko Panyi

items.activity: Check out, drive from Khao Lak into Phang Nga town
items.note: About 1 hour on the inland road. Boats out to the bay leave from around the customs pier and Surakul pier.

items.activity: Board a longtail boat for Phang Nga Bay, through the caves and mangroves
items.note: A private charter runs roughly THB 1,980–3,500 per boat depending on group size — you can negotiate at the pier.

items.activity: Stop at Khao Phing Kan and Ko Tapu (James Bond Island)
items.note: The pointed limestone peak from the 007 film — the classic photo spot of Phang Nga Bay.

items.activity: Lunch at Ko Panyi, a Muslim village out in the sea
items.note: A village built on stilts over the water, with seafood restaurants, a floating football pitch and souvenirs.

items.activity: Head back to shore, rest up, then get ready to go your separate ways
items.note: If you have time to spare, stop by the cave temples near Phang Nga town.
Phuket is about 1 hr 30 min, Krabi about 2 hr. Anyone heading back north should leave around now to avoid driving at night.

blocks.title: About the Phang Nga Bay boats
blocks.html: Boats out to Phang Nga Bay come as group tours or as private longtail charters. If there are several of you, a charter works out better value and lets you set your own schedule — prices start around THB 1,980 per boat for 2 people and go up with the group size. The tide affects whether you can pass through some of the caves, so ask the boatman about timing before you agree, so you don't miss anything.

blocks.text: Where to eat along this route

blocks.html: Eating along this route is fun, because it takes in Ranong's food, southern dishes in Takua Pa, and Khao Lak seafood. These are the places and dishes people talk about most at each stop — slot them into the plan by meal. All prices are rough estimates, and it's worth checking opening days before you go.

items.name: Sam Si Seafood (Bang Sak, Khao Lak)
items.blurb: A seafood spot on the main road in the Bang Sak area, strong on fresh ingredients and bold southern flavours. The dishes people order most are crab fried rice, seafood tom yum and fish fried with fish sauce — an easy lunch stop as you drive into Khao Lak.
items.meta: Bang Sak, Khao Lak · on the main road
items.price: ~THB 120–300 per dish · group meal depends on order

items.name: Krachang Khao Lak (floating seafood)
items.blurb: A newer floating seafood restaurant at Thap Lamu pier, done up in a cafe style with views of mangroves, sea and mountains. Good for a relaxed dinner in the breeze, with fresh seafood since it's right by the pier.
items.meta: Thap Lamu pier · open 15:00–22:00, closed Tue
items.price: By weight · group meal ~THB 300–600 per person

items.name: Cotton Cafe (La Vela Khaolak)
items.blurb: A cafe in the beachfront La Vela resort, known for its croissants and bakery. Good for ducking out of the afternoon sun with a coffee and a sea view during your Khao Lak day, in a nicely designed setting.
items.meta: Khao Lak · inside La Vela resort

items.name: Valhalla Cafe (Khao Lak sea-view cafe)
items.blurb: A newer sea-view cafe that many people rate as the best view in Khao Lak. It's not large and seating is limited, and it gets busy in the evening — if you want a good view spot, go before the sun's gone.

items.name: Southern food in Takua Pa old town
items.blurb: The old-town quarter of Takua Pa has southern restaurants and local coffee shops set in old buildings — yellow curry, khua kling, southern fried noodles, bold home-style flavours at fair prices. Good for breakfast or lunch before you head into Khao Lak.

items.name: Seafood and made-to-order in Khura Buri
items.blurb: Khura Buri is a small fishing district with made-to-order restaurants and seafood at local prices in town. Good for a day-one lunch as you drive south, before you reach Khao Lak.

items.name: Seafood restaurants on Ko Panyi
items.blurb: On Ko Panyi, out in Phang Nga Bay, there are seafood restaurants for lunch during the boat tour — fresh catch from the waters around the island, in a floating-village setting you won't find elsewhere. Prices are set for tourists, though.
items.meta: Ko Panyi, Phang Nga Bay · tour lunch

items.name: Ranong dim sum breakfast (before you set off)
items.blurb: Before leaving Ranong to head south, start the morning with dim sum at a well-known spot like Ranong Ocha — prawn har gow, siu mai, steamed buns and a hot Ovaltine. A breakfast that sets you up for the long drive.
items.meta: Ranong old town · opens early, fills up fast
items.price: Around THB 20–40 per basket · ~THB 100–150 per meal

items.name: Souvenirs from Ranong and Phang Nga
items.blurb: Before leaving Ranong, pick up roasted cashews, shrimp paste and dried shrimp for the road. Phang Nga has skewered shrimp, chilli pastes and processed seafood around Khao Lak and Phang Nga town — save these for the end of the trip.
items.meta: Souvenir shops in Ranong–Khao Lak–Phang Nga town

blocks.html: Since this is a one-way drive, your stay doesn't have to be in the same place the whole trip — base yourself where the day's sights are, and it'll flow best. Spend the first night around Khura Buri or Takua Pa, and the second night on Khao Lak's long beach.

items.name: Night 1 — Khura Buri/Takua Pa
items.blurb: Small, affordable stays in town, good for an overnight on the way through. If you're heading out to the Surin Islands the next morning, pick somewhere near Khura Buri pier for an easy early start.

items.name: Night 2 — Khao Lak beachfront
items.blurb: Khao Lak has beachfront resorts across a range of levels — like La Vela or The Haven, with big pools and beach views. A good place to settle in and enjoy the sea breeze before Phang Nga Bay.

items.name: Onward from Phang Nga
items.blurb: End the trip at Phang Nga Bay and carry straight on to Phuket or Krabi, since they're close. If you'd rather spend another night in Phang Nga town, there are hotels there too — quiet and good value.

items: 2 nights' accommodation — a twin room split two ways runs around THB 500–1,500 per person per night, depending on level; the Khao Lak beachfront night is higher.
3 days of food — around THB 800–1,500 if you have seafood and a cafe or two along the way.
Fuel and tolls — about 230 km; fuel works out to roughly THB 500–800 per car for the whole trip, split by the number of people.
Phang Nga Bay boat — a longtail charter is around THB 1,980–3,500 per boat, which comes to a few hundred per person once split.
Surin/Similan island trip (if you do it) — a day trip out and back is around THB 1,800–3,000 per person, including park fees.
Souvenirs — up to you, starting in the low hundreds.

blocks.title: Driving this route safely
blocks.html: The Ranong–Phang Nga stretch of Phetkasem switches between two lanes and four, with winding hill sections and frequent rain. Fill up before leaving the bigger towns, as petrol stations are spread out in places. Avoid driving at night — there's little street lighting and plenty of trucks — and allow time to stop and rest every 1–2 hours to stay safe.

faq.q: How long does it take to drive from Ranong to Phang Nga?
faq.a: From Ranong town to Phang Nga town is around 230 kilometres, about 3.5 hours straight through on Highway 4 (Phetkasem). But we'd suggest breaking it into stages, since there are waterfalls, old towns and Khao Lak to stop for along the way — which is why this plan is laid out as an unhurried 3 days and 2 nights.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Ranong and Phang Nga?
faq.a: The clear-sky, calm-sea window on the Andaman coast is November to April. If you're set on visiting the Surin or Similan islands, you have to come while the national parks are open — mid-November to mid-May. Outside that, the parks are closed and you can't go out to the islands, but mainland spots like the waterfalls, old towns and Phang Nga Bay are still doable year-round.

faq.q: Can I fit in a Surin or Similan island trip on this route?
faq.a: Yes, but you'll need to set aside extra time. Boats to the Surin Islands leave from Khura Buri pier, and the Similans leave from Thap Lamu pier at Khao Lak. A day trip out and back takes the whole day, so if you want an island day we'd suggest extending to 4 days, or swapping the Khao Lak day for an island day instead — and check the parks' latest opening dates before you book.

faq.q: What kind of boat is best for Phang Nga Bay, and how much does it cost?
faq.a: There are group tours and private longtail charters. If there are several of you, a charter works out better value and lets you set your own schedule — prices start around 1,980 baht per boat for 2 people and go up with the group size. The boat takes you to Ko Tapu, Khao Phing Kan and Ko Panyi. Ask the boatman about the tide times before heading out, since they affect whether you can pass through some of the caves.

faq.q: Can I do this trip without a private car?
faq.a: You can, but it's not as smooth as driving yourself, since the sights are spread out and there's little public transport between districts. There are minivans and buses on the Ranong–Phang Nga–Phuket route that drop you in each town, but getting from there to the smaller sights is awkward. If you're not driving, we'd suggest hiring a car with a driver for parts of the trip, or using specific tours like the island trips and Phang Nga Bay.
